newsitem.title: CANADA: Canada's Martin sees relief for taxes/RRSPs - report.
newsitem.headline: Canada's Martin sees relief for taxes/RRSPs - report.

text.p: Canadian Finance Minister Paul Martin's top priorities include tax relief for lower and middle-income Canadians and raising the maximum annual contributions allowed for tax-sheltered private retirement plans, Toronto's Globe and Mail newspaper reported on Monday.
The annual limit for Registered Retirement Savings Plans has been frozen at C$13,500 a year until 2003 despite earlier plans to raise the limit gradually to C$20,000.

"At some point...you'll see those limits increased, but...we're only going to do it when we can do it in a way that is fair to all the other stakeholders in the country, so that we can move ahead on all fronts at once," Martin told the Globe in an interview after the G7 summit in Denver.
"We have always said we want (the private pension) system to be improved."
But he said his first priority, once the budget deficit was eliminated, would be giving income tax relief to lower and middle-income Canadians, the Globe reported.

"My own personal view, at the present time, is that very clearly relieving the tax burden for middle-income and lower-income Canadians...has got to be where we first begin," Martin was quoted as saying.
Liberal Prime Minister Jean Chretien has said the federal budget should be balanced within two years.
Any budget surplus would be split, with half going to revitalize social programs and the rest for debt reduction and tax relief, the Liberals have said.
